newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian fund release fails to lift share trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian fund release fails to lift share trade.

text.p: The much-awaited release of funds to Nigeria's government agencies failed to stem the current run on shares at the stock market on Tuesday, dealers said.
The all-share index dropped to 8089.72 from 8109.95 on Monday.
The News Agency of Nigeria on Monday said the Finance Ministry had released 32.8 billion naira ($397.6 million), from the 89 billion naira ($1,072 million) budgeted for capital projects in 1997.
"The release may be good for business but the impact on stock trade is doubtful because the market itself is going through a slow process," one dealer told Reuters.

He and others blamed the development on other market issues such as current poor corporate results, the state of the Nigerian economy and operators' reluctance to fully warm up to the automated clearing system introduced in April this year.
Blue chip stocks were weaker on persistent selling.
Nestle was 50.50 naira, down 20 kobo, the same drop as Cadbury which closed at 33.00 naira.
Coca-Cola bottler Nigerian Bottling Company fell 10 kobo to 49.70 naira. Nigerian Breweries dropped 15 kobo to 16.50 naira and Flour Mills was at 15.65 naira, down five kobo.
Conglomerate Lever Brothers closed 18 kobo lower at 23.80 naira while UAC slipped to 13.65 naira, shaving off 15 kobo.
West African Portland Cement Company (WAPCO) and Ashaka Cement were respective 10 kobo and five kobo losers at 59.90 naira and 12.35 naira.
Petroleum marketers continued their downward drift.
Unipetrol fell 30 kobo to 63.40 naira while African Petroleum, at 49.50 naira, and Agip at 14.30 naira, lost 20 kobo apiece.
Increasing interest in Guinness saw its price gain 20 kobo to 9.00 naira.
NAL Merchant Bank, experiencing positive market sentiments after posting an improved financial result, climbed 30 kobo to 9.61 naira. AIICO Insurance hit 16.00 naira, rising by 28 kobo.
Traders said speculation was responsible for the positive movements in Smithkline Beecham shares which ended 10 kobo up at 5.50 naira.
Afribank was one kobo stronger at 3.87 naira and IPWA, the paint maker, closed at 1.90 naira, up three kobo. -- Lagos newsroom +234 1 263 03 17
